title: Chapter 9: Tripura Biodiversity — Flora, Fauna & Protected Areas

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Phayre's Langur is designated as the State Animal of Tripura.
The Agar Tree is recognized as the State Tree of Tripura.
Clouded Leopard and Elephant are major key wildlife species found in Tripura.
Tripura's ecological diversity is protected across designated flora, fauna, and protected areas.

blocks.content: Despite its small area (10,486 sq km), Tripura has significant biodiversity as part of the Indo-Burma Biodiversity Hotspot. Approximately 60% of the state is under forest cover — one of the highest proportions in India. The forests range from tropical moist deciduous in the plains to subtropical hill forests in the highlands.

cells: Hollong, Garjan, Teak (plantation), Rubber, 60+ bamboo species, 150+ orchid species
Phayre's Langur (state animal), Clouded Leopard, Elephant, Leopard, Gaur, Sambar
Green Imperial Pigeon (state bird), Great Pied Hornbill, Pied Falconet, various migratory species
King Cobra, Python, various vipers; gharial in rivers historically
Freshwater fish in rivers; mahseer, catfish; Rudrasagar Lake fish
Elephant, leopard, Phayre's Langur, bear, sambar; buffer around Dumbur reservoir; important elephant corridor
Phayre's Langur (state animal) — one of the best places to see this rare primate; gaur, sambar, barking deer, porcupine; near Muhuri River
Famous for Clouded Leopard and Spectacled Monkey (Phayre's Langur); also has a zoo and botanical garden; nearest wildlife sanctuary to Agartala; very popular tourist spot
Smallest protected area; primarily a botanical reserve; rare plant species
State zoo; clouded leopard breeding programme; adjacent to Sepahijala WLS

items: Phayre's Langur (Trachypithecus phayrei) is the state animal of Tripura
A leaf monkey (colobine); distinctive white circles around the eyes — also called 'spectacled langur'
IUCN: Endangered
Best place to see in India: Trishna Wildlife Sanctuary, South Tripura — has one of the largest populations
Also found in Gumti WLS, Rowa WLS, forest areas throughout Tripura
Threatened by habitat loss and hunting; Tripura has launched conservation programmes
Tripura is one of the few states with a confirmed population of Clouded Leopards (Neofelis nebulosa)
Found in Sepahijala Wildlife Sanctuary; captive breeding programme at Sipahijola Zoo has been successful
IUCN: Vulnerable; very secretive and rarely photographed in wild
Tripura's Sepahijola Zoo achieved captive breeding milestones — important for species conservation
Frequently asked state symbol: Phayre's Langur is the State Animal of Tripura.
Frequently asked botanical symbol: Agar Tree is the State Tree of Tripura.
Key wildlife species associated with Tripura include the Clouded Leopard and Elephant.
Wild Elephants are found in Tripura; frequent human-elephant conflicts occur
Gumti Wildlife Sanctuary is a key elephant habitat; elephant corridors connect with Assam and Bangladesh (historically)
Estimated population: 60–90 wild elephants in Tripura
Human-elephant conflict is a serious problem; elephants raid crops in North Tripura and Dhalai
Agar (Aquilaria malaccensis) is the state tree of Tripura and one of the most economically valuable trees in the world
Source of Agarwood (Oud) — the resinous heartwood formed when the tree is infected by a fungus
Agarwood is one of the most expensive natural products in the world — used in perfumes, incense, and traditional medicine
Tripura is a major source of Agarwood in India; significant cultivation and wild populations
International trade in Agarwood is regulated under CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species)
The Agar Industry is increasingly important for Tripura's economy; government is promoting Agarwood cultivation
